body: Private blood-testing startup Theranos was valued at ~$9 bn (2014) on claims that a finger-prick device could run hundreds of tests. In Oct 2015 John Carreyrou (WSJ) revealed it ran most tests on modified commercial analysers and that its own device was unreliable; regulators sanctioned its lab; the company dissolved in 2018. Elizabeth Holmes was convicted on four fraud counts and sentenced to 11.25 years (Nov 2022). Visible flags: (1) no peer-reviewed data or independent validation; (2) a board of statesmen/generals rather than lab scientists; (3) extreme secrecy and NDAs, employee turnover; (4) investors (family offices, media owners) without healthcare diligence; Walgreens' partnership skipped proper testing; (5) founder charisma substituted for evidence. Lesson for listed markets: deep-tech/biotech claims need third-party validation (peer review, regulatory approvals, customer audits); a 'celebrity' board is a governance red flag, not comfort. Included briefly as a private-market case; no listed tickers.

data.early_signals: no peer-reviewed data; non-expert board; secrecy
data.lesson: Demand independent validation of technical claims
data.spotted_by: John Carreyrou (WSJ); whistleblowers Tyler Shultz, Erika Cheung
